notes: All six lesson bodies and all 70 questions fully read, including every option, explanation, worked example and answer index. This is full semantic review with targeted primary-source checks and direct mathematical reasoning, not exhaustive sentence-to-source mapping. Counts are logged correction groups, not a fabricated count of all factual claims.

All 32 lesson Python fences and 13 quiz Python fences executed. The abstract backtracking template received an explicit binary-choice fixture; the duplicate-skipping fragment received its declared candidate/start context. Intentional negative-factorial quiz failure was checked as RecursionError. No Scheme, C, package-solver, production codec, database or regex performance benchmark was run.

Primary harness passes 52,035 assertions: 626 binary tree shapes; three-symbol arrays through length seven; powers and signed Karatsuba including a 15,000-bit regression; 1,000 closest-pair sets checked against all pairs; subset/permutation/combination oracles; positive-denomination subsets; N-Queens counts through 12, all small placements; Sudoku givens and all units; all 64 A/# grids and binary words through length seven; 1,200 interval schedules against subset enumeration; Huffman optimality against full binary tree depth enumerations; and 800 knapsacks against subset/extreme-point oracles. Finite tests supplement proofs; they do not prove general bounds.

Supplemental harness passes 3,015 assertions: seeded random coin counterexample, displayed combinatorial arithmetic, 3,000 half-approximation checks against exact subsets, a strict minimum-conflicts interval counterexample (best four versus forced three), 92 eight-queen placements with 12 dihedral classes, and Sudoku 729 candidate rows/324 constraints. An initial random search found no interval counterexample; a manually constructed example then validated the claim. No content change is inferred from a harness search failure.

Seven visible gap notes cover four lesson omissions and three quiz omissions: unsupported N-Queens timing, Sudoku call-count comparison, regex timings, currency-design prevalence, permutation runtime/memory and knapsack runtime. Regex timing appears separately in lesson and quiz. No unsupported empirical figures retained as measurements.

Targeted source sections read, not entire books or all pages of retrieved papers. Pearson canonical-coin result was checked only in publisher search abstract; direct article retrieval failed. Kozen-Zaks PDF text was garbled, so the first-page theorem abstract was visually read from the downloaded document; strict c3+1 < x < cm+c(m-1) domain preserved. N-Queens construction theorem checked in academic teaching material and direct small-instance enumeration, not the original 1969 paper.

Unavailable old Guido blog recovered from author archive; one closest-pair lecture failed and another academic lecture was retrieved. Historical MP3 paper failed; LAME source verifies Huffman implementation. Original diagrams and shared overrides untouched. Global link reachability data is inherited from docs/audit-links.json and is not treated as semantic proof.

Algorithmic O(1) operations are scoped to the stated cost model; Python arbitrary-precision integers, floating-point geometry, hashing, recursion depth and materialised output are described separately. No claim of formal verification or universal performance is made.
